title: Extracting total RNA from Caenorhabditis elegans using phase-lock gel separation tubes
author: Cristian Riccio
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.5sug6ew
materials: Continue with Nanodrop and RNA Broad Range Qubit. Info on phase lock tubes: Quantabio, 5PRIME, Phase Lock Gel Heavy, 2ml – 200, catalog number: 2302830, store at 15-25 degrees.Ordered more from VWR International Ltd., ref. 733-2478
Info on phase lock tubes: Quantabio, 5PRIME, Phase Lock Gel Heavy, 2ml – 200, catalog number: 2302830, store at 15-25 degrees. Ordered more from VWR International Ltd., ref. 733-2478

steps.title: Collect worms from plate
steps.instruction: Start with a 90 mm NGM plate containing 3300 C. elegans worms, add M9 buffer to the plate, and pipette the worms into a 14 mL Falcon tube.

steps.title: Wash worms with M9
steps.instruction: Add M9 to the Falcon tube, centrifuge at 2000 rpm in a large centrifuge, remove the supernatant, and repeat the add‑M9‑centrifuge‑remove cycle three times.

substeps.instruction: Add M9 to resuspend the worm pellet.
Repeat the three‑step wash two more times (total of three washes).

steps.title: Lyse worms in TRIsure
steps.instruction: Add 750 µL TRIsure (Bioline, catalog number BIO‑38033) to each sample, mix, and store the tubes at –80 °C until further processing.

steps.title: Decontaminate work area
steps.instruction: Wipe the bench with RNaseZap or 0.1 % SDS prepared in DEPC‑treated water.

steps.title: Freeze‑thaw cycles
steps.instruction: Perform five freeze‑thaw cycles on the TRIsure‑worm lysate: dip the tube in liquid nitrogen for 3 min, then dip in room‑temperature water until no ice remains; repeat five times. For 24 samples, three liquid‑nitrogen tanks are sufficient.

steps.title: Check carcass removal
steps.instruction: Inspect the lysate; if many worm carcasses remain, add an additional 750 µL TRIsure and split each sample into two tubes.

steps.title: Pre‑spin phase‑lock tubes
steps.instruction: Place heavy phase‑lock gel tubes in a centrifuge and pre‑spin at 21 130 × g for 1 min at 4 °C.

steps.title: Add chloroform (first)
steps.instruction: Transfer the TRIsure‑worm mixture to a pre‑spun heavy phase‑lock gel tube, add 150 µL chloroform, shake by hand until an emulsion forms, and incubate 10 min at room temperature. Do not store chloroform in plastic; use it directly from the glass jar.

steps.title: Centrifuge first extraction
steps.instruction: Centrifuge the tube at 21 130 × g for 5 min at 4 °C.

steps.title: Add chloroform (second)
steps.instruction: Add 400 µL chloroform using a manual repeater pipette equipped with a 10 mL combitip (to avoid spillage).

steps.title: Centrifuge second extraction
steps.instruction: Centrifuge at 21 130 × g for 5 min at 4 °C. After this spin the gel moves to the middle, the pale phase is on top and the green phase is at the bottom.

steps.title: Precipitate RNA
steps.instruction: Decant the upper (pale) aqueous phase into a DNA LoBind tube, leaving a small amount to avoid pulling gel. Add 500 µL isopropanol (1:1 with the aqueous phase) and 1 µL glycogen (optional; omit if RNA is abundant). Mix by inversion and incubate 5 min at room temperature for abundant RNA (or –80 °C for 1 h for low‑quantity RNA). Do not incubate on ice or in a freezer to avoid salt precipitation.

steps.title: Pellet RNA
steps.instruction: Centrifuge at maximum speed (≈21 130 × g in an Eppendorf 5424 R) for 30 min at 4 °C.

steps.title: Prepare hot DEPC water
steps.instruction: Heat DEPC‑treated water to 80 °C in a heat block (will be used for resuspension).

steps.title: Discard phase‑lock tubes
steps.instruction: Place the used phase‑lock gel tubes into a dedicated waste bin.

steps.title: Wash RNA pellet with ethanol
steps.instruction: Remove the isopropanol supernatant, then wash the pellet four times with 900 µL cold (kept on dry ice) freshly prepared 70 % ethanol. For each wash: add ethanol, centrifuge 5 min at 4 °C, 21 130 × g, and remove the ethanol. Do not let the pellet dry. (Note: 80 % ethanol is preferred for small‑RNA extraction, but 70 % ethanol is used for total RNA.)

steps.title: Remove residual ethanol
steps.instruction: Using a P1000 pipette, remove the bulk of the ethanol (~1000 µL), then finish with a P20 pipette (~20 µL). If the pellet detaches, centrifuge again for 2 min. Keep the Eppendorf tubes with the opening facing inward to locate the pellet easily.

steps.title: Air‑dry pellet
steps.instruction: Place the tubes in a biosafety hood and air‑dry for 10 min at room temperature. A tiny residual ethanol drop does not affect RNA quality.

steps.title: Resuspend RNA
steps.instruction: Add 50 µL 80 °C DEPC‑treated water (maximum volume accepted by the Sanger facility) to each pellet and flick the tube for 1 min. For many samples, handle 3–4 tubes together and scrape the tube bottoms on a rack back‑and‑forth.

steps.title: Heat and spin RNA
steps.instruction: Heat the resuspended RNA at 80 °C for 1 min in a heat block, then briefly spin down.

steps.title: Store on ice
steps.instruction: Transfer the tubes to an ice bath (water ice) for short‑term storage. (Ice is optional; RNA quality remains high without it.)
